modules.title: Networking Fundamentals
modules.theory: Introduction to TCP/IP, DNS, and HTTP protocols.
modules.lab: Analyze simulated PCAP files to identify plain-text credentials.
modules.opSec: Theory of network monitoring: How defenders detect anomalous traffic and how threat actors attempt to blend in with normal traffic.

modules.title: Command Line Basics
modules.theory: Basic Linux commands, file permissions, and navigation.
modules.lab: Navigate a simulated file system to find hidden 'flag' files.
modules.opSec: Understanding logging mechanisms (e.g., .bash_history) and the theoretical concepts of log evasion.

modules.title: Reconnaissance & OSINT
modules.theory: Using public sources to gather information about a target domain.
modules.lab: Use simulated WHOIS and DNS enumeration tools.
modules.opSec: Concept of origin masking: Why threat actors use VPNs and Tor to mask their IP addresses during reconnaissance.

modules.title: Basic Network Scanning
modules.theory: Understanding how port scanners (like Nmap) identify open services.
modules.lab: Run a simulated SYN scan against a target network.
modules.opSec: Scan detection: How Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) detect rapid scanning and the theory behind stealth/slow scanning.

modules.title: Introduction to Cryptography
modules.theory: Differences between encoding, encryption, and hashing.
modules.lab: Crack simple MD5 hashes using a simulated dictionary attack.
modules.opSec: Offline vs. Online attacks: Why attackers prefer to exfiltrate hashes and crack them offline to avoid account lockout mechanisms.

modules.title: Web Architecture
modules.theory: How web servers and browsers interact (HTML, JS, Cookies).
modules.lab: Inspect simulated web page source code for hidden comments and developer API keys.
modules.opSec: User-Agent tracking: How defenders use browser fingerprints to track activity and how attackers modify User-Agents.

modules.title: Social Engineering Basics
modules.theory: Psychological manipulation techniques used in phishing.
modules.lab: Identify red flags in simulated phishing emails.
modules.opSec: Sender verification evasion: The theory behind spoofing email headers and how SPF/DKIM/DMARC defend against it.

modules.title: Web Application Proxies
modules.theory: Using proxies (like Burp Suite) to intercept and modify HTTP requests.
modules.lab: Intercept a request and modify a price parameter before it reaches the server.
modules.opSec: TLS interception: Understanding how HTTPS protects transit data and the concept of certificate pinning.

modules.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
modules.theory: How untrusted user input can execute JavaScript in a victim's browser.
modules.lab: Inject a payload to trigger an alert box in a simulated search field.
modules.opSec: WAF evasion theory: How Web Application Firewalls detect common payloads and the theoretical methods attackers use to encode payloads.

modules.title: SQL Injection (SQLi) Basics
modules.theory: Understanding how user input alters SQL queries.
modules.lab: Use a basic 'OR 1=1' payload to bypass a simulated login portal.
modules.opSec: Query obfuscation: Theoretical discussion on how attackers use SQL comments or alternative encoding to bypass basic signature detection.

modules.title: Authentication Attacks
modules.theory: Techniques for guessing credentials and session management flaws.
modules.lab: Perform a simulated brute-force attack against a login endpoint.
modules.opSec: Rate limiting evasion: How attackers theoretically use distributed proxy chains (rotating IPs) to bypass rate limits.

modules.title: Directory Traversal
modules.theory: Exploiting improper sanitization of file paths.
modules.lab: Read the /etc/passwd file on a simulated vulnerable server.
modules.opSec: Payload normalization: How servers normalize paths (e.g., ../) and how attackers theoretically bypass these filters.

modules.title: Network Sniffing
modules.theory: How ARP works and how it can be abused for Man-in-the-Middle attacks.
modules.lab: Simulate intercepting traffic between two virtual nodes.
modules.opSec: MAC Address masking: The concept of MAC spoofing to hide physical device identities on local networks.

modules.title: Basic Privilege Escalation
modules.theory: Understanding file permissions and how SUID binaries run as root.
modules.lab: Exploit a misconfigured SUID binary to gain a root shell.
modules.opSec: Process hiding: Theoretical concepts of how rootkits hide malicious processes from system administrators.

modules.title: Advanced SQL Injection
modules.theory: Extracting data when the application does not return SQL errors.
modules.lab: Use simulated time-based payloads to infer database contents letter by letter.
modules.opSec: Traffic timing anomalies: How defenders detect time-based attacks and how attackers introduce jitter to avoid statistical detection.

modules.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
modules.theory: Forcing a server to make requests to internal resources.
modules.lab: Exploit a simulated webhook to access an internal metadata API.
modules.opSec: DNS rebinding: Theoretical concept of using dynamic DNS to bypass SSRF filters during the time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) window.

modules.title: Buffer Overflows
modules.theory: Memory architecture, the stack, and how overwriting the Instruction Pointer (EIP) works.
modules.lab: Simulate overwriting a buffer to execute a pre-placed shellcode.
modules.opSec: Exploit mitigation theory: Understanding ASLR and DEP, and the theoretical concepts of ROP (Return-Oriented Programming) chains to bypass them.

modules.title: Active Directory Attacks
modules.theory: Understanding Kerberos authentication and Service Principal Names (SPNs).
modules.lab: Extract simulated ticket-granting service (TGS) tickets for offline cracking.
modules.opSec: Event Log monitoring: How defenders use Windows Event Logs (e.g., Event ID 4769) to detect Kerberoasting, and how attackers attempt to blend in.

modules.title: Command Injection
modules.theory: Exploiting applications that pass unsanitized input to system shells.
modules.lab: Inject terminal commands into a simulated ping utility.
modules.opSec: Out-of-band (OOB) exfiltration: Conceptually how attackers use DNS queries to exfiltrate data when direct outbound connections are blocked.

modules.title: Advanced Evasion
modules.theory: How Antivirus/EDR uses signatures and heuristics to detect malware.
modules.lab: Simulate obfuscating a known payload to bypass a static signature check.
modules.opSec: In-memory execution: The theory behind fileless malware and how attackers execute code directly in RAM to avoid touching the disk.
